title: Freshfields partners explore carve-out of AI unit worth ‘billions’, leaked emails reveal
key_facts: Partners at Freshfields, a large international law firm, are considering opening its AI unit to outside investment, per a Financial Times report.
They think a carve-out could create a company worth 'billions'.
The talks were revealed by a leaked internal email exchange.
Global managing partner Alan Mason and Ethan Klingsberg, US corporate and M&A co-head, discussed placing the AI business in a separate legal entity.
quote_evidence: are considering opening up the firm’s AI unit to external investment, discussing carve-out options that they believe could create a company worth ‘billions,’ according to a report in the Financial Times.

why_it_matters_hint: Shows a law firm treating its AI tools as a business worth selling to outside investors.
